figures.title: The nested loops
figures.caption: The inner loop performs the task. The outer loop improves the task performer. They communicate through cases, traces, graders, budgets, and rules.
figures.alt: Two concentric cycles: a fast agent cycle inside a slower product-evaluation cycle, connected by task, grader, trace, budget, and rule artifacts.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: The grader ladder
figures.caption: Use the least magical grader that can answer the criterion.
figures.alt: Six ascending grader steps from an environment oracle to expert judgment, with increasing interpretive scope and cost.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Four kinds of truth
figures.caption: The output tells you what the agent said. The workbench tells you where to verify it.
figures.alt: A fluent agent output points to four external evidence workbenches: repository tests, database state, expert criteria, and cited source passages.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Anatomy of an eval task
figures.caption: A prompt is one field in a task contract.
figures.alt: A task contract flows from purpose through setup, input, execution limits, expected evidence, and owner metadata, with harness and version dependencies shown below.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Annotated trace and first departure
figures.caption: The visible failure is at the end. The actionable departure is often earlier.
figures.alt: A four-lane trace timeline marks an unsafe inference at event three and a visible duplicate booking change at event six.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: pass at k versus pass to the k
figures.caption: A nearly certain demo and a worse-than-even user journey can come from the same per-task score.
figures.alt: Three candidate attempts produce 98.44 percent pass at three, while three required sequential tasks produce 42.19 percent journey reliability, both from a 75 percent per-task rate.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Evaluation funnel
figures.caption: Fast checks protect iteration; deeper evidence protects release; production starts the next cycle.
figures.alt: Five narrowing evaluation gates move from local smoke checks through PR, nightly, held-out audit, and production rollout, which loops back to discovery.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Dataset lifecycle
figures.caption: An eval suite is maintained evidence, not a permanent monument.
figures.alt: A circular dataset lifecycle runs from production failure through candidate review, capability and regression suites, audit, then refresh or retirement.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Ownership map and clocks
figures.caption: Centralize the mechanics. Keep the meaning of good with the domain. Put both on a clock.
figures.alt: Eval artifacts sit at the center of product, engineering, and domain owners, supported by platform, data science, and risk, with recurring review clocks.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: The first thirty days
figures.caption: A month can establish one minimum viable eval loop; consequence sets the release pace.
figures.alt: Four weekly columns cover discover, encode, measure, and operate, ending in controlled shadow or production evidence with artifacts accumulating across the month.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Demo question versus product questions
figures.caption: The demo is a valid answer to a smaller question.
figures.alt: One spotlighted demo case asks whether the system can work once, while varied production cases ask about truth, repetition, safety, variation, and learning.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Discovery sample versus measurement sample
figures.caption: Use enriched samples to discover categories and representative samples to estimate rates.
figures.alt: Production feeds a failure-enriched discovery basket and a probability-sampled measurement basket with different questions.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Composite grader
figures.caption: Do not let beautiful communication average away an unauthorized action.
figures.alt: State, authorization, action history, communication quality, cost, and latency feed a structured result, with hard gates separated from soft quality.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Four attacks on an executable grader
figures.caption: Every executable oracle needs cases that test the oracle.
figures.alt: Four quadrants show narrow passing, overconstraint, side-effect escape, and environment tricks as attacks on executable graders.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Judge calibration pipeline
figures.caption: Calibration decides where the judge may be trusted, not whether it is universally good.
figures.alt: Expert labels flow through adjudication, development data, a judge, category confusion matrices, bounded scope, and drift audit.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Paired comparison
figures.caption: The average says plus ten. The 26 disagreements explain the change.
figures.alt: One hundred paired tasks divide into 62 both pass, 18 new-only, 8 old-only, and 12 both fail, emphasizing the 26 disagreements.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Clustered evidence
figures.caption: Fifty rows from five documents are not fifty independent worlds.
figures.alt: Fifty question dots are grouped inside five documents to show shared error families rather than independent observations.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Offline-to-online outcome chain
figures.caption: An offline metric is a proxy until production validates the arrows.
figures.alt: Offline criterion flows through near-term behavior to product outcome, with each arrow labeled hypothesis and a production experiment feeding evidence back.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Production evidence layers
figures.caption: Independent evidence layers fail differently.
figures.alt: Six offset evidence layers with different holes cover runtime guards, asynchronous graders, samples, risk review, delayed outcomes, and experiments.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Eval failure wheel
figures.caption: Measurement needs monitoring, adversaries, owners, and an exit plan.
figures.alt: Eight eval failure modes surround the statement that the eval is part of the system.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.

figures.title: Four-case comparison card
figures.caption: Four benchmarks, four locations of truth, four different maintenance problems.
figures.alt: Four vertical benchmark cards compare artifact, strongest truth, grader risk, and maintenance lesson for SWE-bench, tau-bench, HealthBench, and DeepResearch Bench.
figures.source: Original diagram for Measure Twice, Prompt Once; Evidence Workshop visual system.
